chunks: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abu Said al-Hasan b. Ali al-Adawi narrated to us. He said: Suhayb b. Abbad b. Suhayb narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Al-Sadiq Jafar b. Muhammad narrated to us from his forefathers from al-Husayn b. Ali (peace be upon them):
The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) made adjudications with an oath alongside a single witness, and Ali (peace be upon him) made adjudications likewise in Iraq.

key_terms.الشاهد الواحد: single witness — Islamic jurisprudence discusses whether one witness plus an oath suffices for a ruling
key_terms.اليمين: oath — a sworn statement used as evidence in judicial proceedings

ai.seo_question: Can a judge in Islam make a ruling based on one witness and an oath?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq (AS) from Imam al-Husayn (AS), establishes a legal precedent from the Prophet (s) allowing judicial rulings based on one witness accompanied by an oath. Imam Ali (AS) later applied this same principle during his governance in Iraq, demonstrating the continuity of Prophetic legal methodology through the Imams.
